correctness.rationale: Substituting the exact secant relation \(y_{k,i}=q s_{k,i}\) into the published coordinate update makes the unprojected metric a convex combination of \(q\) and \(u_{k,i}\), so projection is inactive when both lie in \([m_L,m_U]\). The error recurrence is therefore exact and multiplicative. The infinite product vanishes if and only if \(\sum_k s_{k,i}^2\) diverges, proved by the standard two-case comparison for \(\log(1+t)\). The exponential bias lower bound follows from \(\log(1+t)\le t\). The two-objective quadratic realizes \(g(x)=q(x-a)\) exactly, and the Q-linear path-energy bound follows from a geometric-series estimate.

value.rationale: The diagonal variable metric is presented as a main new component of DVM-R3TCG and is empirically credited with improving performance. The theorem identifies a previously unstated structural tradeoff created by the fixed regularizer: the same damping that stabilizes metric changes also limits cumulative curvature learning, and a rapidly convergent trajectory can preserve nonzero metric bias forever even under noiseless exact secants. The exact iff criterion and quantitative lower bound give a concrete design diagnostic for regularization and excitation, rather than a routine algebraic restatement.
